title: Chapter 2 : Basic Concepts of Logic
content:
👋 ሰላም የEthioFresh ተማሪዎች!
እንኳን ወደ Logic Chapter 2 (Basics of Logic) በሰላም መጣችሁ! በዚህ ክፍል የ Logic መሠረታዊ ፅንሰ-ሃሳቦችን፣ Argument ምንድነው? Premise እና Conclusion እንዴት ይለያሉ? Indicator words ምንድናቸው? የሚሉትን ዋና ዋና ነጥቦች ከነምሳሌዎቻቸው እና ከፈተና ጥያቄዎች ጋር አዘጋጅተናል። በጥንቃቄ ተከታተሉ፣ ለፈተና 100% ዝግጁ ትሆናላችሁ! 🚀

1. What is the Meaning of Logic?

The word logic comes from the Greek word logos, which means sentence, discourse, reason, truth, and rule. In its broader meaning, logic is the science that evaluates arguments and the study of correct reasoning. It could also be defined as the study of methods and principles of correct reasoning or the art of correct reasoning.

Key Definitions of Logic:
  • Logic is a science that evaluates arguments.
  • Logic is the study of methods for evaluating arguments—more precisely, whether the premises of arguments adequately support or provide good evidence for the conclusions.
  • Logic is a science that helps to develop the methods and principles that we may use as a criterion for evaluating the arguments of others and as a guide to construct good arguments of our own.
  • Logic is the attempt to codify the rules of rational thought. Logicians explore the structure of arguments that preserve truth or allow the optimal extraction of knowledge from evidence.
  • Logic is one of the primary tools philosophers use in their inquiries. The precision of logic helps them to cope with the subtlety of philosophical problems and the often misleading nature of conversational language.
Logic (ሎጂክ) የሚለው ቃል የመጣው Logos ከሚለው የግሪክ ቃል ሲሆን ትርጉሙም ንግግር፣ ምክንያት፣ እውነት ወይም ሕግ ማለት ነው። በአጠቃላይ Logic ማለት የአስተሳሰብንና የክርክሮችን (Arguments) ትክክለኛነት የምንመዝንበት ሳይንስ ነው።

😅 የካምፓስ ምሳሌ: ዶርም ውስጥ ጓደኛህ "ዛሬ ሌክቸረሩ አይመጣም ምክንያቱም ካፌ ቁርስ ላይ አላየሁትም" ቢልህ፣ የሰጠህ ምክንያት (Premise) እና የደረሰበት መደምደሚያ (Conclusion) ምን ያህል ይገናኛሉ? ብለህ ስትመዝን Logicን እየተጠቀምክ ነው ማለት ነው! ☕

2. What is the Benefit of Studying Logic?

"Logic sharpens and refines our natural gifts to think, reason and argue." (C. S. Layman)

We use logic in our day-to-day communications. As human beings, we all think, reason and argue. The ability to think and reason well might partially be a matter of natural gift. However, whatever our natural gifts, they can be refined, improved and sharpened; and the study of logic is one of the best ways to refine one's natural ability to think, reason and argue.

Major Benefits of Logic:
  • It helps us to develop the skill needed to construct sound (good) and fallacy-free arguments of one's own and to evaluate the arguments of others.
  • It provides a fundamental defense against the prejudiced and uncivilized attitudes that threaten the foundation of a civilized and democratic society.
  • It helps us to distinguish good arguments from bad arguments.
  • It helps us to understand and identify the common logical errors in reasoning.
  • It helps us to understand and identify the common confusions that often happen due to misuse of language.
  • It enables us to disclose ill-conceived policies in the political sphere, to be careful of disguises, and to distinguish the rational from irrational and the sane from the insane.
Logic የመማር ዋናው ጥቅም በደፈናው ሰዎችን አምኖ ከመቀበል ይልቅ ምክንያታዊና አሳማኝ አመለካከት እንዲኖረን ማድረግ ነው። አላስፈላጊ ስህተቶችን (Fallacies) እንድንይዝ፣ የሰዎችን ሃሳብ እንድንመዝን እና የራሳችንን ሃሳብ በግልጽ እንድናቀርብ ይረዳናል።

3. What is an Argument?

Argument is a technical term and the chief concern of logic. In logic, an argument is defined as a group of statements, one or more of which (the premises) are claimed to provide support for, or reason to believe, one of the other (the conclusion).

Note: In logic, an argument does not mean a mere verbal fight or dispute as one might have with a friend or family member.

Key Structural Features of an Argument:
  1. An argument is a group of statements: To qualify as an argument, a passage must combine two or more statements.
  2. Statements vs Non-statements: A statement is a declarative sentence that has a truth-value (either true or false).
Examples of Statements (They have Truth-Value):
  • Dr. Abiy Ahmed is the current Prime Minister of Ethiopia. (True)
  • Mekelle is the capital city of Tigray Region. (True)
  • Ethiopia was colonized by Germany. (False)
Examples of Non-Statements (No Truth-Value - Cannot form Arguments):
  • Would you close the window? (Question)
  • Let us study together. (Proposal)
  • Right on! (Exclamation)
  • I suggest that you read philosophy texts. (Suggestion)
  • Give me your ID Card, Now! (Command)
Argument (ክርክር) በ Logic ትርጉሙ የቃላት ጩኸት ወይም ፀብ አይደለም! Argument ማለት የአረፍተ ነገሮች ስብስብ (Group of Statements) ሲሆን፣ ቢያንስ አንድ Premise እና አንድ Conclusion አለው።
ለ Argument መስሪያነት የሚያገለግሉት Statements (እውነት ወይም ሐሰት ሊባሉ የሚችሉ አረፍተ ነገሮች) ብቻ ናቸው። ጥያቄ፣ ትእዛዝ፣ ወይም ጥቆማ Argument ሊሆኑ አይችሉም! ❌

4. Components of an Argument: Premises and Conclusion

The statements that make up an argument are divided into premise(s) and conclusion. An argument contains at least one premise and one and only one conclusion.

  • Premise: A statement that sets forth the reason or evidence given for accepting the conclusion of an argument.
  • Conclusion: A statement that is claimed to follow from the given evidence (premise). It is the main claim that the argument is trying to establish.
Example 1 (Good/Well-supported Argument):
1) All Ethiopians are Africans. (Premise 1)
2) Tsionawit is Ethiopian. (Premise 2)
Therefore, Tsionawit is African. (Conclusion)
Example 2 (Bad/Poorly-supported Argument):
1) Some Africans are black. (Premise 1)
2) Zelalem is an African. (Premise 2)
Therefore, Zelalem is black. (Conclusion)
* Premise (መነሻ ሃሳብ/መረጃ): ለመደምደሚያው ማስረጃ ሆኖ የሚቀርብ ሃሳብ ነው። (አንድ ወይም ከዚያ በላይ ሊሆን ይችላል)
* Conclusion (መደምደሚያ):** ከመረጃው የሚደረስበት ዋና ነጥብ ነው። (አንድ Argument የሚኖረው አንድ Conclusion ብቻ ነው!)

መልካም (Good) Argument የምንለው መረጃው መደምደሚያውን በትክክል ሲደግፍ ሲሆን፣ መረጃው በቂ ካልሆነ ግን Bad Argument ይባላል።

5. Techniques of Identifying Premises and Conclusions: Indicator Words

The first technique to identify premises and conclusions is looking at indicator words.
📌 Conclusion Indicators:
(The statement immediately following is the conclusion)
  • Therefore
  • Wherefore
  • Accordingly
  • Provided that
  • It must be that
  • We may conclude
  • Entails that
  • Hence
  • It shows that
  • Whence
  • Thus
  • Consequently
  • We may infer
  • It implies that
  • As a result
  • So / It follows that
📌 Premise Indicators:
(The statement immediately following is a premise)
  • Since
  • As indicated by
  • Because
  • Owing to
  • Seeing that
  • Given that
  • As
  • For
  • In that
  • May be inferred from
  • Inasmuch as
  • For the reason that
⚠️ Special Case: "For this reason" vs "For the reason that"
* "For this reason": Comes after the premise and before the conclusion. (Premise ➡️ for this reason ➡️ Conclusion)
* "For the reason that": Comes immediately before the premise. (Conclusion ➡️ for the reason that ➡️ Premise)
💡 Exam Hint:
አንድ Argument ውስጥ Indicator word ከሌለ መደምደሚያውን ለማወቅ እራስህን 3 ጥያቄዎች ጠይቅ፡
1. What single statement is claimed to follow from others?
2. What is the arguer trying to prove?
3. What is the main point in the passage?

6. Arguments Without Indicators & Passing Comments

Sometimes arguments contain no indicator words at all. In such cases, the main point the arguer tries to establish is the conclusion.

Example:
"Our country should increase the quality and quantity of its military. Ethnic conflicts are recently intensified; border conflicts are escalating; international terrorist activities are increasing."

Standard Form:
(P1) Ethnic conflicts are recently intensified.
(P2) Border conflicts are escalating.
(P3) International terrorist activities are increasing.
Thus, (C) Our country should increase the quality and quantity of its military.

Passing Comments: Passages containing arguments may also include sentences that are neither premises nor conclusions. If a statement is merely a passing comment and does not support the conclusion, it should be excluded from the argument structure.
አንዳንዴ አንቀጽ ውስጥ ለትርጉም ማሟያነት ገብተው ነገር ግን Premise ወይም Conclusion ያልሆኑ ተጨማሪ አረፍተ ነገሮች (Passing comments) ሊኖሩ ይችላሉ። እነዚህን ነጥብ ሳንቆጥር ዋናውን መረጃና መደምደሚያ ብቻ መለየት አለብን።

📝 Exam-Style Practice Questions

Q1: Which of the following sentences can serve as a statement in a logical argument?
A) Please turn off the light.
B) Ethiopia is a landlocked country in the Horn of Africa.
C) How many students passed the exam?
D) Let us go to the library.

👉 Click for Answer & Explanation
Answer: B
Reason: Choice B is a declarative sentence that has a truth-value (True). Choices A, C, and D are a command, question, and proposal respectively, which have no truth-value.
Q2: Identify the premise and conclusion in the following argument:
"You should avoid any form of cheating on exams because cheating on exams is punishable by the Senate Legislation of the University."

👉 Click for Answer & Explanation
Premise: Cheating on exams is punishable by the Senate Legislation of the University.
Conclusion: You should avoid any form of cheating on exams.
Reason: The statement following the premise indicator "because" is the premise.
Q3: True or False: An argument can have multiple conclusions if it has multiple premises.

👉 Click for Answer & Explanation
Answer: False
Reason: By definition, an argument can contain one or more premises, but one and only one conclusion.
